title: Taste, smell and the experience of food
intro: Flavor combines taste with smell, temperature and texture. A blocked nose can make meals seem bland even when tongue receptors work. A change in flavor therefore does not always mean loss of taste itself.

sections.heading: Detecting dissolved substances
paragraphs: Saliva carries food chemicals to taste receptor cells in taste buds. Nerves relay their signals to the brain; a dry mouth can interfere with eating and the experience of flavor.

sections.heading: Basic qualities
paragraphs: Sweet, sour, salty, bitter and umami are recognized taste qualities. Different tongue areas can detect multiple qualities; the familiar map with a separate exclusive zone for each taste is misleading.

sections.heading: Smell and sensation
paragraphs: Aromas reach the nose from the mouth during eating. Chili heat is mainly irritation sensed by other nerves, not an additional basic taste. Temperature and texture also affect enjoyment.

sections.heading: Caring for changes
paragraphs: Maintain oral hygiene and discuss persistent changes, dry mouth or medicines with a professional. Do not stop medicines yourself or compensate automatically with much more salt or sugar.

sections.heading: Safety and assessment
paragraphs: Loss of flavor can affect appetite and weight; assessment may include the mouth and sense of smell. Do not use taste to decide whether food or chemicals are safe; follow storage rules and warning labels.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira notices soup tastes dull during a cold. She distinguishes blocked smell from tongue damage rather than adding excessive salt.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben develops persistent altered flavor after a medicine change. He asks for a review instead of stopping treatment alone.
